stem: A nurse is removing a contaminated gown and gloves after patient care. Which principle is most important when doffing this PPE?

options.A: Keep the gown and gloves on until after leaving the patient-care area so contaminated surfaces are handled only in the hallway.
options.B: Remove and discard the PPE before leaving the patient-care area, use a technique that avoids contaminating skin or clothing, and perform hand hygiene after removal.
options.C: After removing the gloves, handle the contaminated front of the gown freely because bare hands are no longer at risk from the gown surface.
options.D: Wear the contaminated gown and gloves to the nurses' station and remove them after documentation is complete.

rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices state that PPE other than respirators should be removed and discarded upon completion of the task before leaving the patient's room or care area, and personnel must be trained to remove and dispose of PPE in a manner that protects themselves and others. CDC Isolation Precautions further directs prevention of skin and clothing contamination during PPE removal, and hand hygiene is performed after glove/PPE removal. Carrying contaminated gown or gloves into common areas or touching contaminated gown surfaces unnecessarily increases self- and environmental-contamination risk.
educational_objective: Doff contaminated gown and gloves before leaving the patient-care area, avoid contaminating skin or clothing during removal, discard appropriately, and perform hand hygiene afterward.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; Guideline for Isolation Precautions
source_version_date: Core Practices updated 2024-04-12; Isolation Precautions prevention page updated 2025-01-31
source_locator: Core Practices → Standard Precautions/PPE recommendations 5c, especially removal/disposal before leaving care area and training in safe removal; Isolation Precautions → II.E Personal Protective Equipment and IV.B.1 principles of PPE use.
source_claim_supported: CDC directs removal/disposal of non-respirator PPE before leaving the patient room/care area, removal in a manner that protects personnel/patients/others and prevents skin/clothing contamination, plus hand hygiene after glove/PPE removal.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, printed p. 26, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control → Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis: apply infection-prevention principles including appropriate PPE and hand hygiene.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE removal and hand hygiene

source_original.stem: A nurse is removing contaminated gown and gloves after patient care. Which principle is most important when doffing PPE?

options.A: Use the same CDC example sequence for all PPE ensembles and locations because sequence consistency is the main protection against self-contamination.
options.B: Use the approved doffing sequence, avoid contaminating skin or clothing, discard PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene.
options.C: Touch the front of the gown freely once gloves are removed because it is then considered clean.
options.D: Wear contaminated gown and gloves to the nurses’ station and remove them after documentation.

source_original.rationale: The safety goal during doffing is to prevent self-contamination. CDC provides example sequences, but the exact order can vary with the PPE ensemble and isolation workflow. Staff should use the approved sequence, avoid touching contaminated PPE surfaces to skin or clothing, dispose of PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices — PPE removal/hand hygiene: remove and discard PPE to avoid contaminating skin/clothing and perform hand hygiene; sequence depends on ensemble/workflow. Current CDC Core Practices at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control; Reporting of Incident/Event and infection/safety activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Removed the unsupported generalized claim that the exact doffing sequence 'depends on ensemble/workflow' from the tested construct. Reframed the item around directly sourced CDC principles: remove/discard before leaving the care area, prevent skin/clothing contamination, and perform hand hygiene after removal.

audit_findings.clinical_category: PPE doffing and prevention of self-contamination
audit_findings.source_authority: Official CDC Core Practices and Isolation Precautions guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: Core Practices dated April 12, 2024 and current; Isolation Precautions page dated January 31, 2025; both rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Core PPE removal recommendations plus Isolation Precautions II.E/IV.B.1 directly support removal location, contamination avoidance, disposal, and hand hygiene.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item avoids asserting a universal or variable sequence beyond the sources; every tested action is explicitly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because contaminated gown/gloves should be removed before leaving the patient-care area.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because the gown front/sleeves are contaminated and removal should prevent hand/skin contamination.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because contaminated PPE should not be worn into common work areas.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B incorporates all CDC doffing principles without unsafe carryover of contaminated PPE.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are plausible doffing-location/handling strategies; no numeric or grammar cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN 2026 Safety and Infection Prevention and Control covers PPE and hand hygiene under Standard Precautions.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review specifically removed the weak 'sequence varies' claim and confirmed no second defensible answer remains.
